text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] prod-gpu-pool queue depth spike: 9,824. Autoscaler tried to add capacity but scheduler reported repeated allocation failures. Severity: SEV1. Affected: inference-serving (embeddings + light generation). https://internal.redwood/ops/incident/2200123456

tanya (on-call): Ack. Paging in SRE + infra. I'm grabbing autoscaler + scheduler traces now.

ryan (sre): seeing placement failures with message: 'placement failed: MIG-slice fragmentation prevents packing; requested 4g but node offers 1g/2g mix'. Autoscaler returned nodes but kube-scheduler rejected pod binding.

liam (platform): confirmed. Pool drifted: some nodes were reprovisioned by our partner image with default 1g slices last week. Workloads primarily request 4g or 2g. Approx stranded: 22 full-GPU equivalents across 9 nodes (slices unusable for current requests).

nina (infra): queue ingestion ~360 r/s, backlog 9.8k -> estimated time to catch up without change: 50+ minutes. We're seeing some 429s from rate-limiter and several customer SDK errors.

ops-bot: autoscaler excerpt:
```
[2026-04-02T01:17:04Z] requestScaleUp: desiredNodes=18
[2026-04-02T01:17:35Z] provisionedNodes=18
[2026-04-02T01:17:48Z] scheduler.bindError: allocation failed, no matching nodes for constraints
[2026-04-02T01:18:02Z] abortScale: rolling back ephemeral nodes due to bind failures
```

ryan (sre): that rollback is the core pain. Autoscaler thought we had capacity, but mismatch of MIG profiles prevented binding, so scale was effectively invisible.

jess (cs): FYI two enterprise customers opened tickets and an on-call contact called. I sent a brief note: "We're aware of degraded embeddings performance and 429s; mitigation in progress; ETA 30m for significant improvement."

liam (platform): immediate mitigation options and tradeoffs:
- (A) emergency reprovision: create new nodes with consistent 4g slices and direct workloads there (fastest to reduce 4g queue but expensive).
- (B) live defragment: evict low-priority tasks from fragmented nodes, let scheduler pack; risk: transient errors and evictions may cause retries upstream.
- (C) route heavy embedding traffic to fallback region (higher cost + cross-region latency).

nina (infra): we can spin 12 uniform-4g nodes in ~6m if we bypass quota softchecks. Need on-call approval to override.

tanya (on-call): Proceed with (A) for the short term. Create nodes with 4g slices and add a routing rule to prefer them for 4g requests.

nina (infra): running command:
```
redwoodctl infra provision --pool prod-gpu --count 12 --node-mig-profile 4g --bypass-quota --reason "incident-2200123456 emergency-provision"
```

ops-bot: provisioning started; 6 nodes ready in 3m, remaining 6 expected in 5m.

ryan (sre): while nodes join, we should reduce tail retries and lower client concurrency for non-SLA routes. Also switch background batch to quantized models to free capacity.

liam (platform): applying route throttles and fallback: 
```
redwoodctl routing throttle --route /v1/embeddings --limit 200rps --scope non-sla
redwoodctl routing set-fallback --route /v1/embeddings --variant embed-quant --percent 50 --scope non-sla --reason "emergency-capacity"
```

tanya (on-call): implemented 50% fallback for non-SLA. Monitoring impact.

relic-bot: metric alert: queue depth falling: 9,824 -> 5,100 in 7m after first 6 nodes joined. Median latency down from 18s -> 9s. 429 rate reduced.

liam (platform): additional mitigation: start targeted evictions on the worst-fragmented nodes once new nodes reach Ready and scheduler can place pods. Plan: cordon -> move low-priority pods -> drain -> uncordon. Expected to free additional ~6 GPUs. Risk: brief task restarts.

ryan (sre): agreed. Execute after 10 nodes are ready. I'll coordinate eviction priorities and set pod disruption budgets to minimize churn.

nina (infra): 10/12 nodes Ready now. Kicking off drain plan on nodes: gpu-node-47, gpu-node-52, gpu-node-59.

ops-bot: drain logs:
```
[2026-04-02T01:26:10Z] cordon gpu-node-47
[2026-04-02T01:26:18Z] evict: moved 12 low-prio pods
[2026-04-02T01:26:45Z] drain complete gpu-node-47
```

relic-bot: queue depth now 2,980. Latency median 6.2s. 429s near 0 for enterprise routes. Background batch throughput reduced to prioritize real-time customers.

jess (cs): updated customers: enterprise customers saw degraded performance for ~22 minutes, then improvement after mitigations. We'll prepare a postmortem and timeline for account teams.

ryan (sre): preliminary root cause: unintentional drift in provisioning templates caused heterogeneous MIG slice profiles across pool; autoscaler lacked fragmentation-aware placement logic and rolled back scale-up when binds failed. This left large backlog and stranded GPU slices.

liam (platform): immediate follow-ups created: PLAT-2401 (enforce MIG profile in provisioning pipeline), PLAT-2402 (autoscaler changes -> detect fragmentation and avoid rollbacks by provisioning matching-profile nodes), SRE-1023 (defragmenter orchestration for live consolidation).

nina (infra): ops note: we'll keep the emergency 4g nodes for 48h and schedule a controlled consolidation window next week to rebalance pools. Also adding a watchdog job to detect pool profile drift.

tanya (on-call): handing off watch to ryan for the night. If queue > 3k or any enterprise 5xx/429 occur, escalate to pager.

ryan (sre): ack. I'll monitor placement failures and queue for 2 hours, and will capture all traces for RCA.

jess (cs): draft message for affected customers prepared: short incident summary, mitigation actions, and offer of credit if SLA breach confirmed.

ops-bot: incident status: mitigated -> watching. Closing SEV1 after 40m stable metrics. Will file full RCA tomorrow.

relic-bot: reaction: :white_check_mark: :rotating_light:
